Summary:

A 45-year-old male patient presents with chronic anicteric cholestasis, chronic Budd-Chiari syndrome (BCS) complicating sarcoidosis, diabetes mellitus, hepatomegaly, splenomegaly, elevated γ-glutamyl transferase, alkaline phosphatase, normocytic inflammatory anemia, and raised angiotensin converting enzyme (ACE) levels. Procedures performed include abdominal ultrasound with Doppler, abdominal CT, chest CT, and medications were prescribed for oral prednisolone and warfarin anticoagulation therapy. Follow-up appointments are scheduled with the primary care physician and specialist providers to monitor symptoms and report any changes.

Summary: Patient presents with a left cerebellopontine angle (CPA) lipoma, hearing loss in the left ear with 70% speech discrimination, and no secondary conditions or critical lab abnormalities. The patient was discharged with follow-up instructions to consult an otolaryngologist for further evaluation and imaging.

Summary: The patient has a complex medical history with nonischemic cardiomyopathy and tobacco use. The patient's condition is exacerbated by an ECOG PS 3, with critical lab abnormalities including mediastinal widening, mediastinal lymphadenopathy, cellulitis, neutropenic fevers, and a pseudomonas aeruginosa infection. The patient underwent mechanical cardiac support with an LVAD, mediastinal widening, mediastinoscopy, and pathologic examination of SCLC. The patient was also treated with carboplatin, etoposide, and IV etoposide. Given the patient's prognosis, hospice care and discharge home were initiated, and the patient passed away six months after chemotherapy administration.

Summary:

The patient is a 55-year-old female presenting with carcinoma of the right breast and postradiogenic circumscribed scleroderma (morphea). Secondary conditions include radiodermatitis and cutis edema. Critical lab abnormalities are also present. Adjuvant radiotherapy (RTX) of the right breast and supraclavicular region was performed. Follow-up instructions include regular check-ups, monitoring of affected areas, and avoiding sun exposure.

Summary: A 65-year-old male with a history of IgA nephropathy, diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and end-stage renal disease, along with sensorineural hearing loss, proteinuria, elevated liver enzymes, low platelets, and microalbuminuria, is being discharged. The patient is scheduled for follow-up with a nephrologist.

Summary: A 45-year-old male patient with a history of vascular injury in the neck zone II presented with multiple cervicofacial lacerations. The patient's hemoglobin level was 4.7 mg/dl, blood pressure was 70/40 mmHg, and pulse was 110 beats/minute. CT angiography and angiography via the right femoral artery were performed, followed by stent insertion and surgery to remove hematoma. The patient is instructed to continue antiplatelet medication and attend follow-up appointments at our outpatient clinic.

Summary:

A 55-year-old male with a history of chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) in chronic phase, pancytopenia, and leishmaniasis presented with high leukocyte count, low hemoglobin level, and high platelet count. He was treated with hydroxyurea, imatinib, pentavalent antimonials, and TKI therapy. Follow-up care is essential as needed.

Summary:

A 45-year-old male patient presenting with recurrent pneumonia, lymphadenopathy, CD hyaline vascular type, lymph node enlargement, pulmonary aneurysm, mediastinal and inguinal lymph node enlargement, and pulmonary artery dilation. Key findings include a history of B-symptoms, recurrent pneumonia, and lymph node enlargement. Procedures performed include a computed tomography (CT) scan. Medications discharged include prednisone, azathioprine, colchicine, and rivaroxaban. Follow-up instructions are to follow up with the rheumatology outpatient department.

Summary:

The patient has been diagnosed with central keratitis and a corneal scraping, which identified Acanthamoeba sp. cysts. The patient has been advised to discontinue contact lens use due to the risk of infection. The patient is undergoing treatment with alternating topical fortified vancomycin, ceftazidime, propamidine isothionate 0.1%, and chlorhexidine. Follow-up instructions are not provided in the note.

Summary:

A 45-year-old female patient is admitted to the hospital with pituitary germinoma and central diabetes insipidus. She is also diagnosed with hypopituitarism, hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, polyuria, and hypertonic hypernatremia. Treatment includes MRI scan, hydrocortisone and levothyroxine replacement therapy, water deprivation test, testosterone replacement, and desmopressin (DDAVP) therapy. She is discharged with medications and follow-up instructions to monitor for relapse or progression of residual disease.

Summary: A 78-year-old male patient is presenting with cognitive impairment and AD-like hypometabolic pattern. His primary diagnoses include cognitive impairment and AD-like hypometabolic pattern. He has undergone various diagnostic tests, including MMSE, MoCA-B, CDR, global deterioration scale, cerebrospinal fluid tau, ptau, Aβ1-42 level testing, Pittsburg compound B PET scan, and F-18 fluorodeoxyglucose PET scan. Based on these findings, he is instructed to follow up with a primary care provider for continued management of cognitive impairment and Alzheimer's disease.

Summary: A 35-year-old male presented with pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma, along with fever, headache, and high blood pressure. Surgical removal of the tumor and CT scans for lesion localization were performed. The patient is currently on medications for managing symptoms and is advised to follow up with the healthcare provider for monitoring of lesions and potential further treatment.

Summary: A 20-year-old female patient is undergoing orthodontic treatment for maxillary right canine removal and partial maxillary osteotomy. The primary diagnosis is bone loss, with an apex constrained condition. Follow-up instructions include post-surgical stabilization, continuous arch maintenance, and follow-up evaluations in 2012.

Initial clinical summary:

The patient is a 45-year-old male with a history of chest pain and lightheadedness. His primary diagnosis is exertional chest pain, and his secondary diagnosis is pleuritic chest pain. The patient also has jugular venous distention and muffled heart sounds, which are critical lab abnormalities. No procedures have been performed, and no medications have been discharged. The patient is instructed to follow up for further evaluation and management.

Summary:

A 55-year-old female patient presented with a sodium hydroxide splash injury of the left eye and symblepharon with superficial and deep corneal neovascularization. She also had a corneal epithelial defect, stromal edema, and descemet’s folds. The patient received subconjunctival bevacizumab injections, dexamethasone sodium phosphate drops, tobramycin, prednisone, and daily for ten days. She was also prescribed 1% atropine drops, 1% dexamethasone sodium phosphate drops, 0.3% ofloxacin, and 50mg prednisone daily for ten days. Follow-up is scheduled for 24 months later to assess her VA and clinical condition.

Summary: Patient has stage IV pulmonary adenocarcinoma with CNS metastasis detected through transbronchial needle aspiration biopsy and endobronchial ultrasonography. Mediastinal lymphadenectomy, wedge resection of the lower lobe of the right lung, and immunohistochemical analysis were performed. Follow-up instructions include continued treatment and no further follow-up planned at this time.

Summary: A 55-year-old male with a history of heart failure, renal artery aneurysm, and arteriovenous fistula is presenting with elevated B-type Natriuretic Peptide (BNP) levels. He is undergoing endovascular occlusion procedures and is advised to continue medications, follow a low-salt diet, maintain a healthy lifestyle, and avoid stress or exertion. Follow-up with the primary care physician is scheduled for further evaluation and management of his condition.

Summary:

Patient, [name], presented with Grade 1 oesophageal varices and an elevated ALT value. Liver biopsy revealed cirrhosis without HIV, hepatitis B, or hepatitis C coinfections. Liver biopsy results were as follows:

- HBV-DNA levels at 3.1 ULN: Elevated
- HBV-DNA levels at 5.75 log10: Elevated
- HBV-DNA levels at 9.2 log10: Elevated
- HBV-DNA levels at 5.28 log10: Elevated

Treatment plan includes:

- Lamivudine at 100 mg/day
- Adefovir dipivoxil 10 mg/day
- Pegylated interferon α-2a
- Tenofovir fumarate 300 mg/day

Follow-up instructions include:

- Liver transplantation as the treatment of choice for the patient due to the presence of cirrhosis.

Summary: A 10-year-old patient is presenting with multiple congenital abnormalities, including an abnormal genitalia, double penile and hypospadias, imperforate anus with distended and duplicated bowel loops, and duplicated recto-sigmoid colon. The patient underwent laparotomy, colostomy, cystoplasty, and surgical exploration. Parents are advised to schedule regular follow-up appointments with their primary care physician for monitoring and management of the patient's condition, as well as to discuss any further diagnostic or treatment options if necessary. It is essential to follow a healthy diet and hygiene practices to prevent complications and discomfort.

Summary: Female patient diagnosed with Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS), Ureteral Stones, Behcet's Disease, and Multiple Myoma. Key abnormalities include high Anti-Mullerian Hormone (AMH) levels. Laparoscopic-assisted myomectomy was performed. Medications include Cyclofenil 600 mg/d for 5 days and Chlormadinone Acetate 4 mg/d for 10 days. Follow-up will be scheduled during her next routine visit.

Initial clinical summary for a clinician:

The patient is a 35-year-old female presenting with a paradoxical reaction after initiating isoniazid, rifampicin, ethambutol, pyrazinamide, and levofloxacin for treatment of tuberculosis. Key findings include fever, chills, and chest pain. CT-guided percutaneous lung biopsy was performed to diagnose the underlying condition. Follow-up instructions are to continue anti-tuberculosis therapy as prescribed and monitor for any adverse reactions.

Summary:

A 45-year-old female presents with a 3-month history of a rapidly growing, painless, ulcerated nodule on her left thigh. The patient has been diagnosed with primary cutaneous ALCL. Follow-up is scheduled with an oncology specialist as directed.

Initial Clinical Summary:

The patient is a 58-year-old male with a history of obstructive coronary artery disease presenting with RVOT-VT with chest pain and palpitations. He underwent external cardioversion, resection of the muscular band, coronary artery bypass grafting, and subcutaneous ICD placement.

Key findings include obstructive coronary artery disease, presenting symptoms of RVOT-VT, chest pain, and palpitations. The patient is currently taking aspirin, atorvastatin, digoxin, lisinopril, and spironolactone-hydrochlorothiazide.

The primary and secondary diagnoses are related to obstructive coronary artery disease. The patient's critical lab abnormalities are not mentioned.

The patient is advised to follow up with primary care physician and specialists as needed, continue prescribed medications as directed, monitor symptoms, report any changes, and seek immediate medical attention if symptoms worsen.

Summary: A 55-year-old patient with oral Crohn's disease and angular cheilitis is undergoing external gingivectomy for treatment. Low serum iron and folate levels, and a raised erythrocyte sedimentation rate, indicate the need for vitamin supplements and follow-up hematological tests to monitor the patient's condition. Follow-up instructions include returning for a 15-month check-up and repeating hematological tests to ensure recovery from gingival inflammation.

Summary: A 55-year-old female patient is being discharged after experiencing difficulty flushing the PEG tube and localized PEG-tube site pain. A procedure was performed, and she is instructed to follow up within the next two weeks for follow-up care.

Summary: 
A 55-year-old male patient presenting with a 3-month history of left-sided chest wall mass, which was surgically excised during a right posterolateral thoracotomy procedure. No critical lab abnormalities were detected. Post-operative management includes follow-up with oncology for further evaluation and care.

The patient has been diagnosed with Chronic pain syndrome with failed back surgery syndrome (FBSS) and mixed pain syndrome composed of a neuropathic radicular component in both legs plus a nociceptive component in the lower back. The patient will follow up with the neurosurgical pain clinic for regular reprogramming visits and maintenance of the neuromodulation systems.

Summary:
A 55-year-old male patient has been diagnosed with Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD), Diabetes Mellitus type 2, High cholesterol, and has been experiencing Exertional dyspnea, Visual disturbances, Night sweats, Progressive fatigue, and extremely elevated White blood cell count (220 × 109/L), low Hemoglobin, and dangerously low Platelets. He has undergone Leukapheresis, Chemotherapy and ATRA, and is being instructed to continue regular follow-up and follow-up care.

Summary:

A 68-year-old male patient with poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma of the pancreaticobiliary primary, characterized by squamous features suggestive of a primary pancreaticobiliary origin, presented with a complex set of symptoms. The patient experienced generalized body weakness, difficulty sleeping, abdominal pain, increased thirst with urinary frequency, constipation, elevated leukocytosis, elevated corrected calcium levels, and low vitamin D levels. Additionally, his alkaline phosphatase and phosphate levels were normal, and his kidney function was within normal limits. CT scan, PET-CT, and CT-guided biopsy of the liver confirmed the diagnosis. The patient was subsequently treated with cisplatin and gemcitabine, and he underwent chemotherapy. However, he succumbed to his condition within three months of diagnosis.

Summary:

A 45-year-old male with a history of muscular dystrophy (MD) gene panel and palpitation presented to the clinic. He is also taking systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) medications. A recent ECG and transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) revealed elevated creatine kinase (CK), indicating muscle damage. The patient is advised to continue SLE medications and follow-up with the primary care physician for monitoring. Additionally, he is scheduled for genetic counseling for the COL6A1 variant.

Summary: A 35-year-old female presented with symptoms consistent with ZIKV infection. Additional findings included contact lens intolerance and ZIKV RNA positivity in urine and plasma. Treatment included urine and blood tests for diagnosis and characterization of an arboviral infection, no medications prescribed. Follow-up instructions are to seek medical attention if future concerns related to her condition develop.

Summary: A 62-year-old male patient is admitted with small-cell lung cancer, purulent pericarditis, acute idiopathic pericarditis, reduced white blood cell and neutrophil counts, elevated creatinine and blood urea nitrogen levels, high lactic acid levels. The patient is undergoing urgent transthoracic echocardiography and emergency pericardiocentesis. He is instructed to return home after 8 days and resume chemo-radiation therapy 2 months later.
Summary: Patient discharged home with follow-up in a youth intensive outpatient program (iop) to address non-pharmacological ways to manage PTSD symptoms.

Summary: A 55-year-old male with a history of appendicitis and endometriosis underwent right hemicolectomy, resection of two segments of small intestine, omentectomy, bilateral ovariectomy, and peritoneal resections with HIPEC administration. The patient is now in close outpatient follow-up. The primary diagnosis is invasive low-grade carcinoma of the appendix colonizing appendicial endometriosis, while the secondary diagnosis is appendix colonizing appendicial endometriosis. There are no critical lab abnormalities.

Summary:
The patient has incomplete duplication of the right side with left hydronephrosis and hydroureter. The left kidney shows hydroureter and the right side shows incomplete duplication. The patient is advised to follow up with the physician for regular check-ups as advised.

Summary:

A 22-year-old male with B-cell ALL presented with a relapse in the CNS. Key findings included leukemic blasts with ≥90% blasts in bone marrow, del(22) q11.2, MYC rearrangement in 68.5% interphase cells, and p53 deletion in 52.0% interphase cells. Treatment included induction chemotherapy, double-delayed intensification, maintenance therapy, whole brain irradiation, and whole spine irradiation. Follow-up instructions are not provided in the note.

Summary: A 55-year-old male patient is diagnosed with chronic bronchitis, bronchial anthracofibrosis, and tuberculous pleuritis. He is also experiencing a pleural effusion with high carcinoembryonic antigen levels and granulomatous inflammation. Treatment includes anti-tuberculosis therapy and follow-up with primary care physician for regular check-ups and continued medication as prescribed.

Summary: Patient has bilateral infiltrates consistent with multifocal pneumonia. Key findings include persistent fevers, secondary infections, and critical lab abnormalities. Procedures performed include IV antibiotics, multiple intubations, tracheostomy. Medications discharged include clindamycin, gancyclovir, linezolid, ceftaroline, ampicillin, valacyclovir, and trimethoprim-sulfa. Follow-up instructions include regular medical treatment plan and medication regimen, with a focus on discussing any concerns or changes in symptoms with healthcare provider.

Summary: A 45-year-old male patient is admitted for a complex multi-system disorder involving intermittent headache and hypomnesis, with elevated serum lactate dehydrogenase and cerebrospinal fluid protein. High-dose methotrexate and idarubicin were administered as part of the treatment regimen. Follow-up instructions include continued close monitoring for adverse reactions and potential relapse.

Summary: A 36-year-old male patient with Wilson's disease presents with decayed teeth and generalized gingivitis. The patient has multiple moderate-to-advanced dental caries. A comprehensive treatment plan includes scaling, composite filling, inlay preparation, gold crown preparation, and simple extraction. Follow-up appointments with the primary care physician and regular dental check-ups are recommended.

Summary:

Patient presents with a cardiac hydatid cyst, presenting with dyspnea on exertion and orthopnea. The patient has eosinophilia and has undergone cardiac hydatid cyst surgery. Follow up with her physician for further management.

Summary:

The patient was diagnosed with leiomyosarcoma, a type of cancer, and underwent two surgeries: resection surgery and RFA for a mediastinal leiomyosarcoma. Radiation therapy was also performed as a follow-up. Pain and numbness in the left upper limb and an enhanced solid lesion were reported. The patient is being monitored for further developments and follow-up instructions are to return to his healthcare provider for regular check-ups.

Summary: 
The patient is admitted with bronchial asthma, pneumonic consolidation involving the right lower lobe, surgical emphysema, subcutaneous emphysema, air in the mediastinum, pericardium, and posterior spinal epidural space. The patient's SPO2 is 89% in normal room air, which requires immediate attention. Broad-spectrum antibiotics, inhalation bronchodilators, systemic corticosteroids, and high-flow oxygen are administered. The patient is instructed to continue monitoring his symptoms and follow-up with his primary care physician regularly.

Summary:

A 35-year-old female patient presenting with rheumatoid arthritis and allergic skin diseases. No critical lab abnormalities identified. She received treatment with Agnitundi vati, Valuka Sweda, and Dashanga Lepa. Follow-up instructions include updating her treating physician of any future allergic reactions to Ayurvedic medication, maintaining a record of allergies and medications, and scheduling follow-up appointments as needed.

Summary:
A 25-year-old male presented with multiple diagnoses including Streptococcus salivarius meningitis, Antiphospholipid syndrome, Cerebrospinal fluid leak (CSF-L), Ventriculitis, and Encephalopathy. Key findings included glucose level less than 10 mg/dL, protein level 732 mg/dL, and nucleated cell count of 2764/uL with 87% segmented neutrophils. Procedures performed included lumbar puncture, bilateral endoscopic ethmoid repair with lumbar drain placement, and ventriculo-peritoneal shunt placement. Medications discharged included apixaban. Follow-up instructions include routine monitoring of antiphospholipid syndrome and CSF-L, continuation of apixaban as prescribed, and regular follow-up with primary care provider, otolaryngologist, and neurosurgeon as recommended.

Summary:

A 35-year-old male patient with a history of Sjögren's Syndrome (SJIA) presents with a complex case involving a complicated JIA, polyarthritis, and serositis. Key findings include dilated coronary arteries. Treatment includes IVIG, high dose ASA, IVMP, Low-dose Prednisone, and follow-up appointments with Rheumatology and Cardiology.

Summary: A 45-year-old female patient diagnosed with acute megakaryoblastic leukemia is also experiencing recurrence of metastatic germ cell tumor. Key findings include pancytopenia and elevated total leukocyte and platelet counts. Trephine biopsy and FNA of a cervical lymph node were performed, with medications being administered for daunorubicin and cytarabin. Further follow-up appointments will be scheduled to monitor the patient's condition.

Summary: 
The patient is experiencing obstipation and sigmoid volvulus, along with hypothyroidism and microcytic anemia. The patient's follow-up instructions include a colonoscopy and laparoscopic sigmoidectomy, scheduled for a later date.

Summary: A 45-year-old male presented with a 3-year history of dull, throbbing pain in the lower right quadrant of his jaw. On examination, a palpable, fluctuant lesion was noted on the buccal surface of the mandibular second molar, consistent with an infected dentigerous cyst. The patient underwent enucleation of the lesion and removal of the impacted mesiodens. No medications were prescribed. Follow-up visits with the dental care provider are recommended to monitor healing and ensure proper oral hygiene.

Summary: A 55-year-old male with a history of rectal carcinoma has been diagnosed with significant diffusion restriction in the frontal white matter bilaterally and the splenium of the corpus callosum. He was treated with neoadjuvant chemotherapy and is scheduled for post-discharge follow-up with an oncologist. The patient is instructed to seek emergency care for similar symptoms.

Summary: An 80-year-old female patient presented with a right femur fracture, secondary to osteoporosis, and significant hip pain, swelling, and restricted mobility. Following hemi replacement arthroplasty using a cemented bipolar prosthesis performed via posterior approach, the patient is now asymptomatic and follows up for 1 year post-surgery.

Summary: A 55-year-old male with stage IV non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) presenting with a history of irritable cough and multiple critical lab abnormalities, including elevated AFP, EGFR E19 mutation, MET amplification, and Ki-67 positive index of 70%, has been prescribed a combination of gefitinib, crizotinib, pembrolizumab, and pemetrexed. The patient is undergoing PET-CT and will complete six cycles of chemotherapy with maintenance pemetrexed. Post-treatment, the patient will undergo regular clinical and radiographic follow-ups, and instructions will be provided for medications and treatment.

Summary: 
A 45-year-old male with a history of mesenteric ischemia secondary to atypical fibromuscular dysplasia is admitted with intractable abdominal pain with diarrhea and vomiting. Colonoscopy, small bowel series, and MRA of the abdomen were performed, and suboptimal angioplasty was performed. Medications were discontinued, and follow-up instructions include follow-up with primary care physician within one week of discharge and cardiologist within two weeks of discharge. Dietary instructions include low-fat, low-salt diet and continued adherence to prescribed medications.

Summary: A 25-year-old male patient with Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome, secondary to growth retardation, neurofibromatosis type 1, hemihyperplasia-multiple lipomatosis syndrome, and splenomegaly, is being managed with growth hormone therapy, follow-up evaluations, and venous malformation treatment.

Summary: The patient is a 55-year-old male with a recurrent schwannoma arising from the middle cranial base, resulting in sunken eye and drooping eyelid. He underwent augmenting the eye socket with an autologous ball-shaped graft, correcting the lower eyelid retraction with an auricular cartilage graft, and correcting the upper eyelid ptosis with a fascia lata graft. The patient was advised to avoid touching the affected eye and follow-ups as scheduled.

Summary:

The patient is a 38-year-old female with a history of non-seminomatous germinal tumor (NSGT E-IB) and multiple sclerosis (MS). She is scheduled for left inguinal orchiectomy, subcutaneous interferon β-1a, radiotherapy (44 Gy), and chemotherapy (gemcitabine, oxaliplatin). Follow-up will be at the discretion of the patient's family.

Summary:

Encounter: Type 1 diabetes with absolute insulin deficiency

Key Findings:
- Acute onset of diabetes
- HbA1c levels of 9.6% and 7.4%
- Presence of both conditions

Plan:
- Initiate insulin therapy with premixed biphasic insulin aspart
- Initiate oral antidiabetic agent, miglitol, and ACE inhibitor, aliskiren
- Initiate renin-angiotensin system inhibitor, candesartan
- Follow-up instructions are not provided in the note

Note: The patient's HbA1c levels are elevated, indicating poor diabetes control. The primary diagnosis is type 1 diabetes with absolute insulin deficiency.

Summary: The patient is suspected of organophosphorus poisoning. Key findings include normal laboratory results and no critical lab abnormalities. Procedures performed include atrial blood gas analysis, serum electrolytes, ultrasonography of the abdomen, and CT of the brain. Medications discharged include atropine 5 mg iv bolus, 1 mg hourly infusion, and parenteral hydration. Follow-up instructions include a 6-week follow-up.

Summary: A 55-year-old female with a history of breast cancer presented with recurrent ductal carcinoma in situ of the breast. She received a stacked DIEP flap procedure and was advised to undergo a follow-up one-year check-up to ensure the aesthetic outcome is satisfactory.

Summary:

A 55-year-old male patient is diagnosed with myeloid sarcoma, a rare form of cancer affecting the bone marrow. He underwent surgical removal of the mass, followed by radiotherapy and two courses of high-dose cytarabine. No critical abnormalities were found in his peripheral blood or bone marrow, and his karyotype is normal. The patient is currently undergoing follow-up instructions but lacks specific discharge instructions provided in the clinical note.

Initial Clinical Summary:

Patient is presenting with deliberate self-harm and neurological toxicity due to intentional ingestion of a substance. The patient's primary diagnosis is intentional self-harm, while the secondary diagnosis is neurological toxicity. The patient's laboratory results indicate pH 7.36, HCO3- 20 mmol/L, PCO2 24 mmHg, pO2 135 mmHg, Base excess -5, lactate level 2.3, and O2 saturation 100%. The patient has been treated with IV diazepam 5 mg. Follow-up instructions include monitoring liver function and continuing supportive care as prescribed.

Summary:

The patient is presenting with Acute Reversible Cerebral Vasoconstriction Syndrome (ARCSV). The primary diagnosis is related to the IUS, which may have caused vasoconstriction leading to increased mean flow velocities (MFV) in both middle cerebral arteries. The patient is also experiencing complications from the IUS.

Key findings include increased MFV in both middle cerebral arteries and the presence of the IUS. The patient should be monitored closely for any further complications.

The patient is currently undergoing CTA and MRA to assess the extent of the damage and determine the best course of action. Follow-up instructions include adhering to the prescribed course of Nimodipine and following up with the healthcare provider after the prescribed course of treatment for any further instructions.

The patient is a 12-year-old female with a history of carious lesions and talon cusps on the maxillary left and right permanent central incisors. A restoration procedure was performed to restore the carious lesions and correct the talon cusps. The patient is instructed to maintain regular dental check-ups and follow up oral hygiene care at home.

Initial Clinical Summary:

A 45-year-old male patient with a history of pleomorphic angiosarcoma (PAIS) was admitted to the hospital with a pulmonary biopsy for further evaluation. The patient's primary diagnosis is PAIS. The patient's secondary conditions are not specified. The patient's critical lab abnormalities are not reported. The patient has undergone a pulmonary biopsy, and no procedures have been performed. The patient is currently receiving follow-up instructions for the administration of stereotactic radiotherapy on both progressive lesions.

Summary: A 3-year-old child was admitted with hemolytic uremic syndrome and Norovirus GI/G II. The child's laboratory findings included leukocytosis, thrombocytopenia, microangiopathic hemolysis, massive albuminuria, and low complement levels. Treatment involved peritoneal dialysis. The child is instructed to continue regular pediatrician visits and a healthy diet and lifestyle.

Summary:

Patient Details:

- Secondary Conditions: Not applicable.

Summary: The patient is experiencing isolated ACTH deficiency, which has led to low serum cortisol levels, inappropriately low ACTH, hyponatremia, elevated ADH, and hypoglycemia. The primary treatment is pembrolizumab monotherapy, with ongoing care recommended for monthly outpatient appointments.

Summary: A 35-year-old female patient is being managed for Topiramate induced acute myopia, persistent headaches, and normal intraocular pressure. She is advised to attend follow-up appointments with her general practitioner and ophthalmologist, and not to take topiramate again.

Summary:

The patient presented with epigastric pain, vomiting, and a symptomatic cystic lymphangioma originating from the left adrenal gland. Ultrasonography, CT scan, MRI, and CT-guided puncture of the cyst were performed for diagnosis. The final diagnosis was confirmed by histopathology combined with immunohistochemistry. The patient was discharged with follow-up instructions to monitor for any recurrence and return to the outpatient clinic one month after the surgery for further evaluation.

Summary:

A 55-year-old male patient is presenting with gross hydronephrosis (GH) caused by a kidney stone at the junction of the ureter and renal pelvis, accompanied by renal cell transitional cell carcinoma (T2N0M0). The patient also has secondary conditions such as abdominal girth increase, abdominal distension, intermittent nausea, and intractable hiccups. Additionally, the patient is experiencing hypertension and electrolyte imbalance.

A comprehensive evaluation including ultrasonography, computerized tomography (CT), and an isotope kidney scan was performed, and a laparoscopy and open simple nephrectomy were performed to address the underlying conditions.

The patient is currently undergoing treatment with hydronephrolysis fluid drainage, hydrochloride therapy, and is advised to follow a proper diet and maintain regular follow-up appointments with the healthcare professional.

Summary:
A 55-year-old male presented with sinus infection and sinusitis. Key findings include mild fever and normal power and sensation. Procedures performed included dorsal D1 to D8 laminectomy, mid-line myelotomy, total tumor excision, methylprednisolone bolus dose, and 5.4 mg/kg dose of methylprednisolone. Medications discharged include methylprednisolone. Follow-up instructions include monitoring for symptoms and returning for follow-up after 10 days.

Summary: A clinician is writing a clinical summary based on the provided key patient details. The patient has multiple diagnoses, including low-grade neuroendocrine tumor, CLL, and marginal zone B-cell lymphoma/chronic lymphocytic leukemia. Key findings include a low-grade neuroendocrine tumor, and active problems are ongoing chemotherapy and octreotide acetate administration. Follow-up instructions include continuing to follow up with the healthcare provider to monitor the CLL and for any future medical concerns.

Summary: The patient is a 3-year-old with complex congenital heart defects, conductive hearing loss, and malformed ossicular chain. They underwent tympanostomy tube placement at age 3 and middle ear inspection and ossicular reconstruction on the left side. The patient is advised to follow up with an otorhinolaryngologic department for regular audiology testing.

Summary: A 45-year-old male with a history of diabetes, hypertension, and spinal cord injury is admitted with an empyema complicating his partial lung resection for adenocarcinoma. His critical lab abnormality is the detection of Streptococcus caprae in wound culture. He has undergone partial lung resection, irrigation and thoracic drainage, and broad-spectrum antibiotic treatment. He is currently on antibiotic therapy and is instructed to follow up with his primary care physician for regular check-ups.

Summary: A 5-year-old female patient is evaluated for severe craniofacial abnormalities, including ish, scaphocephaly, brachycephaly, and total synostosis. She is also experiencing abnormal craniofacial contour and severe osteolysis. The patient has been prescribed follow-up instructions by her healthcare provider.

Summary:
A 45-year-old male presented with a clavicle fracture and was diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma, a secondary condition. He underwent adjuvant chemotherapy and 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) PET-CT, which revealed high tumor markers. He is instructed to continue with regular follow-up CT scans to monitor the clavicle fracture and ensure no signs of cancer recurrence or metastasis.

Summary: The patient has hypertension, high cholesterol, and coronary artery disease with surgical intervention. The patient has a cough with hemoptysis and chest discomfort. The patient is undergoing a percutaneous approach with a PTFE-covered Jostent GraftMaster for coronary artery disease. The patient is on dual antiplatelet therapy as prescribed. Follow-up is scheduled for the healthcare provider as scheduled.

Summary:

The patient was admitted to the hospital for surgery and was discharged with follow-up instructions to attend follow-up sessions at the outpatient clinic for further medical evaluations.

The patient is presenting with biliary colic and dyspepsia, with secondary conditions of colocolic intussusception and nonnecrotizing intussusception. Abdominal tomography revealed diffuse thickening of the transverse colon wall along a 9 cm segment. The patient underwent left hemicolectomy with end-to-end anastomosis. He is advised to contact his primary care physician for any concerns or questions, and to schedule a follow-up appointment with the surgeon within four weeks post-discharge to monitor the surgical site and assess further symptoms.

Summary: A 45-year-old male patient presenting with jaundice, abdominal pain, and liver cirrhosis underwent emergency liver transplant. He is at risk for complications such as hepatosplenomegaly, esophageal varices, and liver transplant. Follow-up instructions include continuing post-operative care and monitoring for complications.

Summary: Patient is admitted for subdural empyema with chronic subdural hematoma. Treatment includes craniotomy and minocycline for subdural empyema and Brugada syndrome. Follow-up instructions are to follow up with primary care physician for wound healing and monitor diabetes and Brugada syndrome; continue oral minocycline for recommended duration.

Summary:

A 32-year-old female patient presented with multiple congenital anomalies including narrow chest, fused lower limbs and feet, absence of external genitalia, imperforate anus, single umbilical artery, bilateral renal agenesis, absence of both kidneys, ureters, urinary bladder, seminal vesicle, and urethra, and gastrointestinal system ending in a blind loop with meconium. She also has diabetes mellitus in the mother. The patient underwent an autopsy for further examination.

Summary: The patient has a complex medical history with hypertension, a total hip replacement for avascular necrosis, and chronic convulsive syndrome. Additional conditions include autoimmune, infectious, and malignant diseases. There is a critical lab abnormality of necrotizing granulomatous vasculitis. The patient was diagnosed with brain biopsy and is currently on medications for cyclophosphamide and methylprednisolone. Follow-up instructions include regular check-ups with the neurologist as needed.

Summary: The patient presents with altered mental status, hypotension, and fever, secondary to immunotherapy-induced rhabdo. Key lab findings include hyperkalemia, hypercalcemia, and elevated procalcitonin. The patient will follow up with nephrology and oncology as an outpatient.

Summary: Patient presented with acute ordial torsion, underwent laparoscopic appendectomy. Follow-up instructions include contacting primary care physician if experiencing any signs of pain or discomfort.

Summary: A 45-year-old male presented with complaints of low back pain, chest pain, right hip pain, and bilateral foot pain. Initial evaluation revealed normal calcium levels and low phosphorus levels, elevated alkaline phosphatase levels, and high FGF23 levels. No medications were prescribed. Follow-up appointments are recommended.

Initial Clinical Summary:

A 45-year-old male presented with a 2-year history of ICH, initially managed with thrombolytic therapy and recanalization. Follow-up 2 years later revealed no enlargement of the IH, indicating successful treatment.

A 45-year-old male patient presenting with multiple symptoms of Myalgia, leukocytosis, neutrophilia, monocytosis, Multifocal myonecrosis, elevated C-reactive protein, ESR, and elevated creatinine kinase levels. Biopsy of the right tibialis anterior muscle was performed. Prescribed medications include anti-inflammatory drugs, antibiotics, and pain relievers. Follow-up instructions include continuing prescribed medications, maintaining a healthy diet, reporting any worsening symptoms to the primary physician, and taking rest as needed.

The patient has been diagnosed with MSSA infection, bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) with severe aortic regurgitation, and an ascending aortic aneurysm. Additionally, they have been treated for community-acquired pneumonia (CAP). Key findings include elevated white blood cell count, fever, and bacteremia. Open-heart surgery with aortic valve replacement (AVR), ascending aortoplasty, and coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) with left internal mammary artery to left anterior descending artery were performed. The patient is currently on nafcillin for eight weeks and will require ongoing home health follow-up to monitor for complications, including blood tests and symptom evaluation.

Summary: A 35-year-old male patient presented with a dissection of the upper limb for a routine surgical procedure. No primary diagnoses were identified, but the patient is currently stable and no critical lab abnormalities are noted. The patient is instructed to follow up with the primary care physician for any future health concerns.

Summary: 
The patient has Listeria monocytogenes meningitis, presenting with multiple generalized tonic-clonic seizures. Key findings include positive Listeria monocytogenes test results and intraventricular amoxicillin and amikacin administered intravenously and phenobarbitone. Follow-up instructions include outpatient clinic visits, protein-conjugated Pneumococcal and Haemophilus vaccines, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole prophylaxis, and ongoing monitoring for recurrence.

Summary:

This patient is experiencing Borderline Personality Disorder, Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder, and Bulimic Disorder. Key findings include a need for ongoing psychotherapeutic interventions, maintaining a healthy diet and lifestyle, and adhering to a healthy dental hygiene routine. Follow-up instructions include continuing with these interventions and scheduling regular check-ups with a healthcare professional.

Summary: A 55-year-old male patient with stage MCC presented with an enlarging crusting lesion on the anterior chest wall, lymph node–positive stage MCC, and metastatic disease to pancreas and peripancreatic lymph nodes. He underwent wide local excision with bilateral axillary and left neck lymph node dissection and started adjuvant radiation therapy. The patient passed away due to inoperable disease.

Summary: A 55-year-old female patient is diagnosed with nodular infiltrating papillary thyroid carcinoma with metastasis to lymph nodes. Treatment included total thyroidectomy, adjuvant radioiodine therapy, radioactive iodine, sorafenib, and entrectinib. Ongoing monitoring and follow-up are necessary to assess long-term response and potential recurrence.

The patient is a 35-year-old female presenting with systemic disorder and secondary conditions such as fever, weight loss, and malaise. Her lab results include low-grade fever, high-grade fever, and weight loss. A skin biopsy was performed and topical steroids, phototherapy, and medications prescribed were administered. Follow-up instructions include continuing prescribed medications, attending subsequent appointments, and reporting new symptoms.

Summary: A 45-year-old male patient with multiple abrasions and a deep perforated wound of the right eye is in critical condition. The patient underwent an emergency CT scan, which revealed profound bleeding, and an emergency evisceration procedure. The patient is currently on follow-up for regular check-ups and medication.

Initial Clinical Summary:

A 55-year-old male patient presented with symptoms of exertional dyspnea and coughing. Key findings include aortic insufficiency and ascending aortic dilatation, with increased cardiothoracic index and prominent aortic arch on transthoracic echocardiography. The patient is also experiencing exertional dyspnea. Follow-up instructions include consulting a cardiologist for further evaluation and monitoring.

Summary: A 55-year-old male patient was admitted for leukocytoclastic vasculitis (HSP) and a pulmonary infection caused by Staphylococcus aureus and Mycobacterium xenopi. His laboratory results showed elevated C reactive protein, low albumin, and low ferritin. Procedures performed included a post-bronchoscopy sputum examination and a pulmonary aspiration smear. He is currently receiving Colchicin 1 mg to reduce pain and articular swelling and Methylprednisolone 1 mg/kg/day. Follow-up is recommended to monitor for recurrence and assess renal function.

Summary: A 45-year-old female presented with a 3-month history of continuous fever. Following a thorough evaluation, she was diagnosed with complete atrioventricular block and underwent ventricular demand pacing (VVI) pacemaker implantation. The new vegetation attached to the lead was visualized during TEE, necessitating open-heart surgery to remove the vegetation and lead. A new epicardial pacemaker was then implanted. Follow-up instructions include monitoring for complications and adhering to post-operative care instructions.

Summary:

A 35-year-old male with a history of Meralgia paresthetica presented with paraesthesia in the thigh region, primarily affecting the lateral thigh. He was diagnosed with Meralgia paresthetica, a neuropathy involving the lateral femoral cutaneous nerve. A Nerve Conduction Study was performed, and the results were abnormal. The patient was prescribed Pregabalin 75-mg nocte and naproxen 275-mg twice daily. Follow-up instructions are to return to the clinic in 4 months for a follow-up and report complete resolution of paraesthesia without any recurrence.
